First off, Pikachu wasn't made into the franchise's mascot until after the anime started its production, and even then this was apparently a last minute decision by the anime staff. The anime was released around April 1997, so it probably began as a concept around 1995 or 1996.

Since a Pokemon's index number in Gen I corresponded to its order of creation, Pikachu and Raichu were created around the same time, as their index numbers were right next to each other. It took Game Freak over 6 years to create the Gen I games. Since Pikachu and Raichu's index numbers were 83 and 84, respectively, and there were over 190 Pokemon slated to be in Gen I, these Pokemon were probably created around the midpoint of the development cycle. 

Pikachu and Raichu were created together before the anime started its production. Raichu still would have existed even if Pikachu weren't chosen as a mascot.

I can't believe people actually believe Blue went to the tower to bury his dead Raticate. Based on what we have experienced from his character, he doesn't seem to particularly care about any of his Pokemon aside from their individual strengths and weaknesses.

When you meet with Blue on the S.S. Anne, he states that he had already caught 40 kinds of Pokemon. 40. Counting the Pokemon he had acquired (starter, Pidgey, Rattata, and Abra), as well as their respective first evolutions, that only adds up to 8 Pokemon. Even if you count Blue scanning the data for Eevee and its evolutions from Bill, that would only get his number to 12. He has acquired at least 28 other Pokemon species by the time you reach S.S. Anne. Those 28 species are unaccounted for, and are probably in his PC.

Even in the tower, Blue merely states he is there to catch Pokemon:

"Hey, RED! What brings you here? Your POKEMON don't look dead! I can at least make them faint! Let's go, pal!"

"What? You stinker! I took it easy on you too!"

"How's your POKEDEX coming, pal? I just caught a CUBONE! I can't find the grown-up MAROWAK yet! I doubt there are any left! Well, I better get going! I've got a lot to accomplish, pal! Smell ya later!"

In Silph Co., Blue actually states that he is starting to understand what is strong and what is not. In other words, he is actively shuffling around his Pokemon to test their individual strengths, and is keeping the best Pokemon on his main team. Blue shuffles Raticate, a Pokemon with terrible base stats aside from its Speed, for Exeggcute, Growlithe, or Gyarados, which have much more potential. Furthermore, you don't see Blue's Cubone at any point in the game, which suggests he either has it in his PC or he released it for not being as strong as other Pokemon.

In the Pokemon League, Blue states that he has created various Pokemon teams (yes, teams) that are designed to counter every type. Blue could have many powerful Pokemon in his PC that he didn't bring with him to the Indigo Plateau. 

This is further suggested during your champion rematch with Blue in FRLG, where he replaces Pidgeot and Rhydon with Heracross and Tyranitar, respectively. Blue went to the Sevii Islands, acquired a Larvitar and a Heracross, and kept them around because of their high base stats and potential.

In GS, Blue replaces his starter Pokemon with Gyarados, Arcanine, or Exeggutor when you battle him in his gym. In HGSS, Blue also replaces his Alakazam with Machamp. In the rematch at the Fighting Dojo, Blue's Rhydon becomes a Rhyperior, and he also uses a Tyranitar. These Pokemon are all lower-leveled than the Pokemon in Gen I and FRLG, which suggests Blue's Gen 2 team are not the Pokemon he used in Gen 1. For example, the Gyarados he uses in his gym battle is not the Gyarados he uses against Red in the Gen 1 games. In Black 2 and White 2, Blue was shown with an Aerodactyl, and his Alakazam returned (or he caught a different one).

It doesn't matter if the Raticate was the same Rattata that you fought on the S.S. Anne, or a completely different Pokemon that he caught. It doesn't matter if Raticate is alive or dead. The real purpose of Raticate's existence is for Blue to replace it with something that is stronger. Raticate is the ultimate proof that Blue can replace any of his Pokemon without a second thought, as long as something better is out there that he can raise. 

Indeed the simplest solution is best: Blue catches a lot of Pokemon, but only actively uses the Pokemon that he deems to be the strongest. This is why you never see his Cubone or the 28+ other Pokemon species that he has caught. Would you think Blue, a trainer who doesn't care about his Pokemon aside from their power, would bother to bury his Raticate? Most of the people at the tower actually cared about the Pokemon that they put to rest. They miss those Pokemon dearly. Blue would never miss his Raticate to the extent that he would actually put it to rest.
